title: Emit onboarding checklist events from gateway + control plane (API key created, first success, streaming established)
author: Amara Diallo
description:
Context: This PR is part of the Guided Onboarding / First Production Launch checklist work. The checklist progress service needs a reliable server-side signal stream (not SDK-only) to compute step completion and TTFS/TTFP. This change adds server-side emission for a small set of onboarding milestones at deterministic lifecycle points in the API gateway and control plane.

What this adds: (1) Emit onboarding event when an API key is created (control plane). (2) Emit onboarding event on the first successful inference response per tenant (gateway; first 2xx from /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank). (3) Emit onboarding event when streaming is successfully established (gateway; first SSE chunk write succeeds for chat/completions streaming requests). (4) Common library helpers to format events according to onboarding-event-schema-v1 and enforce privacy constraints (no prompt/response text, no IP/User-Agent raw strings; only coarse client tags + hashed identifiers). (5) Best-effort dedupe via idempotency keys to avoid emitting multiple "first" events under concurrent load.

Event names (schema v1): onboarding.api_key.created, onboarding.request.first_2xx, onboarding.streaming.first_established

Notes on behavior / edge cases: - "First 2xx" is tenant-scoped and based on the first successful response observed by the gateway; we do not require a minimum token count. - Streaming established is emitted only for stream=true and only after we successfully write the first SSE payload to the client (to reduce false positives from early disconnects). - Idempotency key strategy: tenant_id + event_name (+ api_key_id for key-created); ingestion is at-least-once, downstream should treat keys as unique. - This PR does not gate emission behind the checklist feature flag; the progress service can ignore events for cohorts not opted in. The intent is to begin collecting baseline telemetry ahead of the UI rollout.

Why server-side: SDK-only instrumentation missed key failure modes (auth mistakes, 429 confusion, streaming disconnects) and is harder to trust across language clients. Server-side emission gives consistent coverage for both native and OpenAI-compat endpoints.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add explicit 401/403 and 429 milestone events + reason codes once schema fields are finalized (tracked separately). - Additional ordering/monotonicity hardening in progress computation (see ENG-5866/PR-28510). - Backfill job for pre-existing tenants (ENG-5844).

Testing: Added unit tests for event payload formatting + idempotency key construction. Added gateway integration tests using a local telemetry sink (assert exactly-once semantics under retry/concurrency). Verified streaming-established event triggers only after first chunk write.

Rollout: Safe to ship; event volume is low-cardinality and low-frequency (first-time milestones). Emission uses existing async telemetry publisher with bounded queue; on publisher failure we log at debug and do not impact request path.
commits: telemetry(onboarding): add server-side event constants + schema validator
control-plane(keys): emit onboarding.api_key.created on key creation
gateway: emit onboarding.request.first_2xx for inference endpoints
gateway(streaming): emit onboarding.streaming.first_established after first chunk write
tests: add integration tests w/ fake telemetry sink and concurrency coverage
docs(internal): add runbook notes for onboarding event payload constraints
changed_areas: services/control-plane/src/api_keys/create_key.ts (emit event after successful key create + commit)
snippets: Streaming hook (simplified): after res.write(firstSseChunk) succeeds -> publisher.publishOnboardingEvent({... event_name: onboarding.streaming.first_established ...})
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry): Can we confirm we are not sending raw user agent strings? Also please ensure route names are normalized (no query params) to avoid cardinality issues.

Amara Diallo (Author): Yep — we only send coarse client tags derived from UA parsing (sdk/openai-compat/unknown + language if detected). Route is normalized to the handler path (e.g. /v1/chat/completions) and we explicitly strip query strings. Added a unit test to lock this down.
Ethan Park (Control Plane): Key-created emission is after DB insert, but do we risk emitting on a transaction rollback? Also do we want api_key_id in payload or only hashed?
Amara Diallo (Author): Emission moved to after commit callback (control-plane supports postCommit hooks). Payload includes api_key_id_hash only; raw api_key_id stays internal. Updated comment + test.
Brian Murphy (API Ergonomics): For first_2xx, do we include which endpoint succeeded? We'll want to correlate to quickstart path (chat vs embeddings).
Amara Diallo (Author): Included normalized route + request_type enum (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Kept it low-cardinality. Added to payload builder + docs comment.
Marcus Lin (Security): Please add an explicit assertion that prompts/outputs are not present, and ensure tenant hashing uses the standard salted hash helper (not ad-hoc sha256).

Amara Diallo (Author): Good call — switched to telemetryHashId() helper (salted + rotation-ready) and added a payload allowlist so only expected fields can be set. No request/response bodies are accessible in the emitter path.
Allison Grant (Observability): Any chance this increases p95 latency? Telemetry publisher should be fully async and non-blocking.
Amara Diallo (Author): Publisher call is fire-and-forget onto bounded queue; on full queue we drop with debug log. Added a micro-benchmark in tests and verified no await on request path.
Logan Wright (Telemetry): LGTM after the hash helper change. Please add label docs in the internal readme for the new topic.
Amara Diallo (Author): Done in the last commit (internal telemetry topic registry).
Chloe Martin (Console): Not directly in my area, but thanks for keeping the schema stable — we’ll depend on these for checklist progress.
merge_summary: Merged into main after approvals; squash commit: telemetry(onboarding): emit gateway/control-plane milestones for checklist progress
release_notes: Internal-only: adds server-side onboarding milestone events (API key created, first successful request, first streaming established) to support Guided Onboarding checklist progress tracking and TTFS/TTFP measurement.
